nodes.label: `forward_auth`
nodes.rationale: Forwarded, X-Real-IP and X-Forwarded-* from the client are not passed to the auth service because a client could forge them; copy_headers are removed when the answer lacks them so clients cannot set Remote-User; copied headers join the cache key so users never share cached responses.

nodes.label: `access_log`
nodes.rationale: Request threads format into per-thread buffers and one background thread writes, so nothing on the request path touches disk; when the writer falls behind, lines are dropped and counted rather than slowing traffic. Reopened automatically after logrotate.

nodes.label: ACME
nodes.rationale: One certificate per site for all its hosts (max 100); HTTP-01 answered from memory on every host so wildcards are refused; renews inside the CA's ARI window or at a third of lifetime; PEM replaced atomically and swapped by the reloader so connections are never dropped.

nodes.label: Certificate selection
nodes.rationale: Selection order: exact site cert or ACME override, matching one-label wildcard site cert override, exact SAN, one-label wildcard SAN, default certificate, otherwise handshake fails. Certificate file reloads preserve connections.

nodes.label: Upstream protocol behavior
nodes.rationale: Omitted policy is H1.1 except h2c implies required H2. Required 2 uses prior knowledge on HTTP and strict H2 on TLS; auto falls back on TLS and uses H1.1 on plain HTTP. h2c with explicit auto/1.1 is rejected.

nodes.label: Path normalization
nodes.rationale: Percent-decode, remove empty/dot segments, resolve dot-dot without crossing root, and preserve trailing slash. File candidates use the already decoded path and preserve literal percent bytes.

nodes.label: String conditions
nodes.rationale: A prefix is a plain string prefix, not a path segment: /admin also matches /administrator.

nodes.label: `concurrency`
nodes.rationale: Counts requests, not connections, so it also limits clients behind a CDN where all connections come from the CDN.

nodes.label: `rate_limit`
nodes.rationale: Sliding-window allowance counts admitted requests. Same-key admission is serialized across workers using fixed small locks. Counts use a fixed 64 KiB sketch and survive unchanged-plugin reloads.

nodes.label: Response-cache identity isolation
nodes.rationale: Original authority including port, copied auth headers, certificate fingerprint, trusted XFH and routing distinguish cached identities; the origin remains responsible for session/cookie privacy.

nodes.label: Response-cache lock

nodes.label: pingora-limits count-min sketch

nodes.label: forward_auth plugin (Authelia, Authentik, oauth2-proxy)
nodes.rationale: Remove copied identity headers absent from the auth response so clients cannot forge them.

nodes.label: instant-acme library
nodes.rationale: Use the library only for the ACME protocol while reusing Pingora HTTP and OpenSSL connectors.

nodes.label: mTLS host mismatch response (421)
nodes.rationale: A separate browser connection is required when SNI and Host do not share the same CA.

nodes.label: mTLS TLS-session identity and resumption isolation
nodes.norm_label: mtls tls-session identity and resumption isolation
nodes.rationale: Bind resumption to the CA fingerprint so verification cannot be bypassed by reusing a session from another identity.

nodes.label: Passive ejection and panic mode
nodes.rationale: Keep trying when all backends are unhealthy instead of failing every request immediately.

nodes.label: Path normalization
nodes.rationale: Equivalent encoded paths must reach the same policy decision.

nodes.label: Per-worker upstream connection pool (group_key)
nodes.rationale: Keep socket readiness on the owning runtime; the trade-off is more idle backend connections.

nodes.label: Per-site plugin chain
nodes.rationale: Waiting plugins pause the chain at their written position; authentication must complete before later rules.

nodes.label: Real client IP (real_ip, trusted peers)
nodes.rationale: L7 policies must act on the visitor identity rather than the Cloudflare TCP peer.

nodes.label: Retries to another backend
nodes.rationale: Do not repeat attempts to the same backend.

nodes.label: server.work_stealing: false (runtime per worker thread)
nodes.rationale: No-steal runtimes suit low-rate HTTP/1.1 origin traffic, saving CPU and moderating p99 at the cost of load balancing between workers.

nodes.label: Fork test procedure (jemalloc needs a space-free target dir)
nodes.norm_label: fork test procedure (jemalloc needs a space-free target dir)
nodes.rationale: Prepare the H2 backport before native Cargo; use a disk target without spaces. One selected deterministic pool regression passed; full-suite counts below belong to earlier fork validation.

nodes.label: Precompressed static files and streaming
nodes.rationale: Small files are read once, while large reads run in the blocking pool to protect request threads.

nodes.label: openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH) root confinement
nodes.rationale: Kernel RESOLVE_BENEATH prevents symlink escape. The fallback walks pinned descriptors with O_NOFOLLOW and rejects all symlinks, including in-root links.

nodes.label: Level-1 response compression (gzip, br, zstd)
nodes.rationale: Compression must not change byte ranges, and already compressed responses are passed through.

nodes.label: keepalive_timeout (idle HTTP/1.1 client disconnect)
nodes.rationale: Bound otherwise unbounded idle connections; client-supplied keep-alive timeouts are not trusted.

nodes.label: upgrade_idle_timeout
nodes.rationale: Use bidirectional idle timeouts and treat an upgraded stream separately from a request body.

nodes.label: WebSocket connection lifetime accounting
nodes.rationale: Hold concurrency until the connection closes; rate limits count the handshake only.

nodes.label: HTTP/2 pool race and local backport (issue 1024)
nodes.norm_label: http/2 pool race and local backport (issue 1024)
nodes.rationale: HTTP/2 upstream makes issue 1024 relevant. Local backport of PR1025 locks release_lock and removes an existing InUsePool entry before reinsertion, preventing duplicate entries retaining idle sockets. Includes a deterministic race test; prepare-vendor.sh applies it idempotently.

nodes.label: Headers conduit adds to client responses
nodes.norm_label: headers conduit adds to client responses

nodes.label: Response compression (gzip, br, zstd, level 1)
nodes.rationale: Level 1, the fastest, as nginx's default; only text-like types and statuses 200/403/404 as with nginx; 206 never compressed since it carries a range of the uncompressed representation; q-values are not weighed.

nodes.label: File responses (ETag, conditionals, ranges, MIME)
nodes.rationale: Files are read off request threads in 128 KiB chunks while the previous chunk is sent; several ranges get the whole file with 200.

nodes.label: force_https and hsts
nodes.rationale: HSTS is added after the plugins' response header changes so a headers plugin cannot remove it; the connection's own scheme counts, so behind a TLS-terminating proxy over plain HTTP no HSTS is added.

nodes.label: headers plugin (request/response set/remove)
nodes.rationale: request changes run after conduit's forwarding headers so they can override them; rules always see the client's original headers; response changes apply to every status unlike nginx's add_header.

nodes.label: Load balancing (round_robin, random, least_conn, ketama hash)
nodes.norm_label: load balancing (round_robin, random, least_conn, ketama hash)
nodes.rationale: hash uses consistent ketama hashing of hash_key (client_ip, uri, path, header:, cookie:) so adding or removing a backend moves only a share of keys.

nodes.label: Client certificates (mTLS)
nodes.rationale: Client certs requested only on SNI names of mTLS sites and TLS sessions kept apart per CA set; requests over a connection made for another host get 421 so clients retry on their own connection; client-sent X-Client-* headers are removed.

nodes.label: Protocol upgrades (websocket, any, off)
nodes.rationale: upgrade: any passes every upgrade with its handshake headers (Tailscale control protocol for headscale, DERP); after 101 the connection closes after upgrade_idle_timeout of silence, max_body_size no longer applies, and the log line is written on close.

nodes.label: Request id (x-request-id)
nodes.rationale: 24 hex digits unique within the process unless a trusted proxy supplied one; logged so a client can quote the id of a failed request.

nodes.label: Request handling order (14 steps)
nodes.rationale: Each step can answer and end the request; waiting plugins (basic_auth, forward_auth) are awaited in place so the written order always holds; requests not rewritten by a proxy rule go upstream with the original un-normalized target.

nodes.label: server_header option (Server: conduit)
nodes.rationale: Sent exactly as written and replaces the upstream's Server header; off/false sends none and lets the upstream's pass. No version is disclosed, unlike nginx/<version>.

nodes.label: Site selection and host routing
nodes.rationale: Exact host beats wildcard, longest wildcard suffix wins; *.example.com does not match the apex; duplicate hosts across enabled sites are an error.

nodes.label: Headers believed from a trusted proxy
nodes.norm_label: headers believed from a trusted proxy
nodes.rationale: X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Host and x-request-id are believed only from real_ip.trusted peers; scheme matching, {scheme}, force_https and hsts still use the connection's own scheme.

nodes.label: Headers sent to the upstream (X-Forwarded-*, X-Real-IP)
nodes.norm_label: headers sent to the upstream (x-forwarded-*, x-real-ip)
nodes.rationale: Leftmost X-Forwarded-For entries come from the client and can be forged, so upstreams should read X-Real-IP or the rightmost entry; on upgrade: any, unused hop-by-hop headers are removed as nginx does.

nodes.label: Cache key and variants
nodes.rationale: Cache identity includes original authority with port as well as normalized routing host, site, scheme and target; copied auth headers, mTLS fingerprint, trusted XFH and routed pool/target contribute. Origins must mark cookie/session-specific responses private. Explicit Vary preserves raw field values, boundaries, q-values and absent/empty.

nodes.norm_label: release build profile choices (unwind, fat lto, mimalloc)
nodes.rationale: Unwinding confines a panic to its Tokio task instead of killing the whole proxy.

nodes.rationale: Avoid 2 MiB huge-page arenas almost doubling idle RSS for a small throughput benefit.

nodes.label: server.write_buffer: 16k

nodes.label: conduit-logo-*-ember.svg / conduit-mark-ember.svg
nodes.rationale: All Ember, readable on both light and dark grounds, for places where the background is unknown such as README previews.

nodes.rationale: The wordmark is converted to paths so no font is needed to display it.

nodes.rationale: Dark source is the reverse logo and the fallback is the Ember logo, so viewers that ignore or misreport dark mode still show a readable logo.

nodes.label: Mark usage prohibitions
nodes.rationale: Do not recolour individual outer lanes, rotate or flip the mark, change the stroke weight, or set the wordmark in capitals.

nodes.label: Admin endpoints (/metrics, /healthz, /status, /cache/purge)
nodes.rationale: No authentication, so admin.listen should be bound to loopback or a management network.

nodes.label: conduit check command
nodes.rationale: Builds the configuration exactly as run would (resolves backends, reads certs, htpasswd and CA files) so errors and warnings surface before deploy; exits non-zero on error.

nodes.label: Runtime snapshots on configuration reload
nodes.rationale: Build a new runtime completely before publishing; each request keeps its snapshot. Certificate store and process-wide settings are published separately, not in one global transaction. Failed reload keeps the active runtime.

nodes.label: Watched files (mtime, inode, size, follows symlinks)
nodes.norm_label: watched files (mtime, inode, size, follows symlinks)
nodes.rationale: Checks follow symlinks so a certbot renewal that swaps a symlink is seen; covers config, certs, ACME files, htpasswd, mtls.ca, rule files, default_site.page and crowdsec.ban_page.

nodes.label: Graceful upgrade (conduit run -d -u)
nodes.rationale: New process takes over the old one's listening sockets over upgrade_sock; needed for start-only settings (listen, admin, access_log.path, server, tls.watch_interval, cache.lock_timeout). systemctl reload runs it.

nodes.label: listen section (http/https addresses)
nodes.rationale: [::] listens IPv6-only so 0.0.0.0 and [::] can be listed together; no cleartext HTTP/2 (h2c).

nodes.label: server section (threads, work_stealing, write_buffer)
nodes.rationale: work_stealing false gives one single-threaded runtime per thread for more req/s and lower tail latency; true evens out heavy long-lived HTTP/2 or WebSocket connections at some throughput cost. transparent_huge_pages trades ~1% throughput for ~2x idle memory. write_buffer lets small responses leave in one write and one packet.

nodes.label: tls section (certs, default_cert, acme_webroot, watch_interval)
nodes.rationale: TLS certs, default_cert, acme_webroot and ACME settings; watch_interval must be positive and fit the runtime clock and is read only at startup.

nodes.label: Strict YAML 1.2 configuration parsing
nodes.rationale: Only true/false are booleans so force_https: yes is an error rather than a silent true; unknown keys and duplicate keys are errors so typos fail conduit check; error messages name line/column but never quote the file because it may hold secrets.

nodes.label: Phase 3 historical stability checklist
nodes.rationale: Six core-stability checklist items were completed historically on 9 November; audit fixes and HTTP/2 upstream followed on 10 November. Krynox is a separate operator-reported run.

nodes.label: Responses conduit generates (status table, HTML status page)
nodes.norm_label: responses conduit generates (status table, html status page)
nodes.rationale: Proxy failures and local answers to unread bodies close the client connection; a client that disconnects early is logged as 499 as nginx does.

nodes.label: proxy action (routing and path rewrite)
nodes.rationale: Upstream path is built from the normalized path so /%61pi/x cannot dodge strip_prefix: /api; the result is percent-encoded per RFC 3986 and the original query appended; a proxy rule only routes, so later plugins still run.

nodes.label: redirect action and placeholders
nodes.rationale: Prefer {request_uri} to keep the query and the client's exact encoding; {path} is decoded and may carry unencoded bytes into Location.

nodes.label: rules plugin (first match wins)
nodes.rationale: Rules are tried strictly in written order, unlike nginx's location specificity, so specific rules go before general ones.

nodes.label: Rust regex crate syntax (linear time)
nodes.rationale: No backreferences or lookaround; in exchange matching is linear-time whatever the input, so a request cannot make a rule slow.

nodes.label: File lookup and try_files
nodes.rationale: The normalized request path is percent-decoded once before plugins and file lookup. Expanded try_files candidates preserve literal percent bytes; segment normalization does not decode them again. strip_prefix matches a segment boundary.

nodes.label: openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH root confinement
nodes.rationale: Files use openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH. When unavailable or blocked, pinned directory descriptors and openat O_NOFOLLOW reject all symlinks, including in-root links; directory listings use /proc/self/fd and omit symlinks.

nodes.label: CrowdSec AppSec (WAF) inspection
nodes.rationale: Runs after every plugin let the request through; sends method, target, headers and client via X-Crowdsec-Appsec-* headers, with the body only when declared, within body_limit (max 64k) and not awaiting 100 Continue; failure_action decides allow/block when no verdict arrives within timeout.

nodes.label: CrowdSec bouncer section (stream-mode decisions)
nodes.rationale: Decisions are pulled in stream mode into an in-memory table, so checking a client is a few hash lookups with no network call on the request path; held decisions keep applying while LAPI is unreachable; captcha is refused like a ban (CrowdSec's fallback for unsupported remediations); only ip and range scopes are used.

nodes.label: Freshness, revalidation, stale serving and cache lock
nodes.norm_label: freshness, revalidation, stale serving and cache lock
nodes.rationale: Concurrent misses wait up to cache.lock_timeout for the first fetch instead of all going upstream; known-uncacheable URLs skip the lock; stale-while-revalidate background fetches are not logged, as with nginx.

nodes.label: Cache storage rules (RFC 9111, stricter)
nodes.rationale: Never stores Set-Cookie, 206 or Vary: *; Authorization requests stored only when the response allows shared caching; the upstream decides what is shared, so per-cookie pages must say private or no-store.

nodes.label: Fixed-size counting sketch
nodes.rationale: Fixed memory per plugin (64 KiB rate_limit, 32 KiB concurrency) whatever the number of clients; may overestimate under heavy load, never underestimate.

nodes.label: Match conditions (match: block)
nodes.rationale: All given conditions must hold; there is no host condition because hosts select sites and each site has its own plugins.

nodes.label: Plugin chain and suggested order
nodes.rationale: First plugin that answers ends the request; suggested order: crowdsec and ip_filter first (cheap, nothing else should see such clients), block_exploits, limits, authentication, then rules for authenticated requests.

nodes.label: State that survives a reload
nodes.rationale: Unchanged pools preserve health/ejection/in-flight state, unchanged limiter plugins preserve counts, CrowdSec decisions and fresh cache survive reload. Changing upstream/protocol does not invalidate fresh cache; explicit purge affects entries present at that time, not in-flight fills.

nodes.label: Response cache (in-memory, per-site cache:)
nodes.rationale: Memory shared by all sites with LRU eviction; sites cache nothing unless they opt in; cache: false is an error.

nodes.label: basic_auth plugin (bcrypt)
nodes.rationale: Move expensive hashing to the blocking pool, bound concurrency, cache successful verification and use decoy verification for unknown users.

nodes.label: body_replace plugin (streaming sub_filter)
nodes.rationale: Keep only the longest pattern minus one byte between chunks, then compress after replacement.

nodes.label: Backend DNS resolution at load time
nodes.norm_label: backend dns resolution at load time
nodes.rationale: Names resolve at startup and reload, not per request; each address is a backend. Failed DNS rejects reload. Default pooled HTTP/1.1; explicit HTTP/2, TLS auto negotiation and cleartext h2c are supported.

nodes.label: Backend selection with fallback
nodes.rationale: When no backend is healthy and un-ejected, any untried backend is used, since trying one beats failing every request when the health checks themselves are wrong; 502 only when none is left.

nodes.label: Upstream pools (named, URL, or inline)
nodes.rationale: Named, URL and inline pools support weighted backends and per-pool http_version and http2_max_streams. h2c URLs imply required HTTP/2; HTTP/1.1 remains the default.

nodes.label: Behavior that differs from nginx
nodes.rationale: Written rule order and cross-certificate SNI selection; different body/timeouts/forwarding defaults. NGINX upstream default is HTTP/1.0 before 1.29.7 and HTTP/1.1 since. Conduit defaults to HTTP/1.1 with optional HTTP/2 and upstream h2c; frontend h2c remains unimplemented.

nodes.label: Certificate rotation and reload under load test
nodes.norm_label: certificate rotation and reload under load test

nodes.label: conduit reverse proxy
nodes.rationale: Runs many sites behind one address from one YAML file and one static binary, with hot reload and zero-downtime upgrades. The design follows Pingora's own model (ProxyHttp hooks, load balancer, background services) rather than imitating nginx. Pre-1.0: tested hard locally, first production sites live November 2026, config may still change before 1.0.

nodes.label: Admin listener (/metrics, /status, /healthz)
nodes.rationale: The unauthenticated administrative listener must remain on loopback.

nodes.label: Atomic certificate rotation and reload
nodes.rationale: Refuse half-written key/certificate pairs and keep serving the previous certificate.

nodes.label: JSON access log (per-worker buffers)
nodes.rationale: Per-worker buffers avoid hot-path contention; full buffers drop counted lines rather than slow proxy traffic.

nodes.label: Pingora 0.9.1 framework
nodes.rationale: Use Pingora hooks and services rather than reproducing nginx internals.

nodes.label: Trusted request IDs (X-Request-Id)
nodes.rationale: Accept client-provided IDs only from trusted peers.

nodes.label: Upstream status (checked 2026-11-09)
nodes.rationale: Dated 9 November upstream survey retained as history. Local H2 backport was validated 10 November; these notes do not assert current upstream release or merge status.

nodes.rationale: 30 default E2E plus four explicit ignored cases (ACME, CrowdSec, slowloris and H2 soak) passed on the final implementation. Actual H2/gRPC streams and audit security regressions are covered.

nodes.rationale: A deadline from the first byte prevents a client from retaining a connection by sending individual bytes slowly.

nodes.norm_label: 5c765c6: daemon readiness handler installed before fork
nodes.rationale: Install SIGUSR1 handling before the child can notify, retain early readiness in an atomic flag and restore the default handler in the child.

nodes.rationale: Use the connection digest address; retain the old check for virtual or overridden stream matching.

nodes.label: 3357c9e: one flush per response batch
nodes.rationale: Coalesce compressed header, body and terminal chunk into one send while preserving explicitly required flushes.

nodes.norm_label: 499f89d: configurable server header on pingoras own responses
nodes.rationale: Build rare generated error responses on demand so process settings and reloads take effect.

nodes.rationale: Avoid one spawned task, timer, oneshot and Arc<Mutex> on every upstream reuse.

nodes.norm_label: 7ffe1c4: whole request header bounded by read_timeout (slowloris)
nodes.rationale: Measure one deadline for the whole header rather than resetting a per-read timeout for every byte.

nodes.norm_label: 9586c10: skip hop-by-hop removal when none present
nodes.rationale: Scan names once before attempting unnecessary removals.

nodes.norm_label: 9c64421: header name case as style plus exceptions

nodes.norm_label: bb3859d: upstream response header handed over without copy
nodes.rationale: Move final headers into response tasks, retaining framing/status and lazily reparsing headers only on demand.

nodes.label: c448eff: CasedHeaderName (no re-parse in insert_header)
nodes.rationale: Retain a parsed HeaderName and its written case instead of converting to text and parsing again.

nodes.label: c4cce19: task_pipe HTTP/1 task channel
nodes.rationale: Replace two general-purpose mpsc channels with a bounded four-slot ring for two futures in the same task.

nodes.label: ecef83b: compression MIME check by prefix
nodes.norm_label: ecef83b: compression mime check by prefix
nodes.rationale: Match known MIME prefixes without regular-expression overhead.

nodes.norm_label: single-node scope and separate ha design

nodes.norm_label: planned generic oidc with authentik and zitadel

nodes.label: Planned optional UI and headless default
nodes.norm_label: planned optional ui and headless default

nodes.label: Revision checks and safe retries
nodes.rationale: One coordinator for UI/API/CLI, expected revisions, file fingerprints, intended-field updates, authorization, serialized writes and idempotency. Reject stale writes and show a conflict; no silent last-writer-wins.

nodes.label: One backend configuration contract
nodes.rationale: UI derives schema/defaults/capabilities from the backend; show desired, active and pending-restart revisions; preserve unrelated fields and redacted secrets.

nodes.label: Planned SQLite management state
nodes.rationale: SQLite is for accounts, sessions, permissions, drafts, history and audit; YAML remains authoritative persisted proxy configuration and runtime requests use memory.

nodes.label: Lightweight UI resource budget targets
nodes.rationale: Initial target is 200 KiB gzip primary JS/CSS, not a measurement. Bound polling/history/log views, distinguish configured protocol from negotiated telemetry and compare UI-disabled/idle/active overhead.

nodes.label: External YAML import and write ownership
nodes.norm_label: external yaml import and write ownership
nodes.rationale: Accepted external edits get revisions; invalid candidates retain the active runtime. Strict concurrent-write guarantees require exclusive live-file ownership and imports via cooperating tools, not arbitrary editor writes.

nodes.label: Next planned authenticated management milestones
